channel.title: Global Supply Chain Bulletin
channel.description: An independent daily briefing on supply chains, energy transition and trade geopolitics.

item.title: Issue 77 — Iran's UN delegation left New York Monday with no deal; Trump says “we blow them up or make a deal”
item.description: Saudi Arabia restarted Red Sea exports from Yanbu after a 17-day halt, its main route around Hormuz; ICE Brent settled at $97.46 on Sept 30, with no deal yet on Hormuz.

item.title: Issue 76 — Brent slides below $100 as Mideast oil exports near pre-war levels, even as Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz reopening offer
item.description: Oil's slide below $100 rippled quickly into cost-sensitive markets: the Baltic Dry Index fell to its lowest close since early September and India's Sensex fell for a second session, even as Adani Ports defied the broader selloff with a 4.5% rally.

item.title: Issue 75 — Iran leans into its Hormuz campaign as transits rebound to 132 a week, and its second drone-seizure claim shifts again
item.description: Monday's Hormuz-driven oil spike rippled through Indian equities: the Sensex slid to a six-month low and IRB Infrastructure hit a fresh 52-week low, even as Escondida's copper-mine standoff and Freeport's delayed Grasberg recovery kept metals markets on edge.

item.title: Issue 74 — Iran's parliament speaker vows Hormuz stays shut as IRGC claims a second US drone seizure and Trump still expects talks this week
item.description: Brent jumped back to $105.76 Monday morning, up 1.38% and briefly topping $106, as Iran's parliament speaker vowed Hormuz stays shut and a fresh, disputed drone-seizure claim added to the sense diplomacy is stalling even as Trump says he still expects talks this week.

item.title: Issue 73 — Trump formally rejects Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, calling it 'unacceptable' as officials eye strikes after the midterms
item.description: BHP is bringing Escondida, the world's largest copper mine, back online in stages after a fatal accident — layering a fresh disruption onto Grasberg's shortfall and keeping Comex copper pinned near its record $6.83/lb even as this week's session eased.

item.title: Issue 72 — Iran offers seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz as Trump reportedly rejects it, eyeing decisive action after the midterms
item.description: Markets read this week's diplomacy first through oil: Brent eased 1.3% to $105.26 and the Sensex rebounded 315 points Friday on hope Iran's seven-day Hormuz offer would hold — before word of Washington's reported rejection even spread.

item.title: Issue 71 — Iranian strike kills Indian seafarer aboard the Cape Dao as Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran and US-Iran talks float a 60-day Hormuz ceasefire roadmap
item.description: The Hormuz fatality rippled straight into India's own markets: the Sensex crashed 1,247.71 points and the Nifty gave up 383.70 as Thursday's oil spike wiped out Wednesday's full rebound in a single session — a reminder how directly Gulf shipping risk now prices into Dalal Street.

item.title: Issue 37 — Bessent's "Economic D-Day" finally lands as "Operation Economic Outcast" — but Tehran gets a grace period, and Hormuz stays nearly empty
item.description: Brent's slide to $92.06 a barrel and the Sensex's 172-point retreat are Monday's real market verdict on the sanctions news — a pattern of "sell the headline" repeating from last week's rally, even as war-risk tanker premiums stay locked at 7.5-10% of hull value and TD3C Gulf-China tanker earnings hold above $520,000 a day regardless of what Washington announces.

item.title: Issue 36 — Iran's Rezaei threatens to halt every drop of Gulf oil as Bessent's “Economic D-Day” sanctions near their 2pm ET unveiling
item.description: Brent's 1.38% Monday dip to $93.09 and the Sensex's 172-point slide to 77,369.11 are the market's own hedge against a sanctions package that hasn't landed yet — a reversal of last week's 5%-plus rally that reads as traders pricing pure uncertainty into the hours before Bessent's 2pm ET unveiling, not any actual resolution, even as Drewry's WCI holds at $4,526 and war-risk tanker premiums stay locked at 7.5-10% of hull value.

item.title: Issue 35 — Iran loses its grip on Hormuz as traffic bleeds into the Omani lane, hours before Bessent's “Economic D-Day” sanctions land
item.description: Brent's climb to $94.39 a barrel and Drewry's WCI holding at $4,526 are the market's own verdict on Hormuz — freight and crude pricing keep the standoff priced in even as Kpler finds merchant traffic quietly rerouting through Oman's coastal lane to dodge Iran's shrinking zone of control.

item.title: Issue 34 — Hormuz standoff drags into the weekend as Brent holds near six-day highs and the UAE's trade freeze with Iran shows no sign of a near-term thaw
item.description: Brent holds just under $94 into the weekend close and Drewry's WCI stays elevated at $4,526, with war-risk premiums still at 7.5-10% of hull value — freight and insurance markets keep pricing in a Hormuz standoff that shows no sign of a near-term thaw.

item.title: Issue 33 — Hormuz traffic collapses to a single tracked transit on Aug 16 as the UAE's total break with Iran deepens and Brent extends its run to $93.86
item.description: Brent has now risen for a sixth straight session to $93.86, and Drewry's World Container Index still sits 4% higher at $4,526 — freight and energy markets are pricing in a Hormuz standoff that PortWatch says fell to just 1 vessel transit on Aug 16, against a 73-a-day baseline.

item.title: Issue 32 — UAE's total break with Iran deepens the Hormuz crisis as a tanker is confirmed seized off Qeshm and weekly transits fall to 73
